observational_status: matched four-case, seven-frame normalized-native M3D-C1 numerical timestep response diagnostic; no experimental machine shot, physical current calibration, segmented electrode controller-in-loop, or validated experimental handoff
successful_milestone: Four matched normalized-native M3D-C1 cases at dt=0.005 completed with exact zero-source field equivalence (0 <= 1e-12), consistent 1004-element mesh, and opposite signed jphi lobes. At t=0.03 e[2]-weighted cancellation remains 79.99% negative / 74.40% positive, and R*e[2]-weighted 79.15% negative / 73.83%. Partial proxy cancellation persists under one time-step halving, but numerical convergence is not demonstrated.
interpretation: At dt=0.005, late-time opposing-lobe response persists, supporting redistribution-like numerical response; however odd-sign symmetry residual changes from 80.11% (dt=0.01) to 57.12% (dt=0.005), a 22.98-percentage-point change, and positive signed proxy shifts from 9.184e-5 to 6.569e-5. This substantial timestep sensitivity weakens quantitative convergence and sign-symmetry claims. One additional matched dt=0.0025 refinement is justified before interpreting physical response.
followup_scope: One bounded second dt-halving matched normalized-native M3D-C1 audit (dt=0.0025 vs dt=0.005, twelve vs six steps to t=0.03), preserving source mode 4, amplitudes, gate, mesh, solver physics, frozen gates; compare e[2] and R*e[2] lobe cancellation and odd-sign symmetry at aligned time samples; no physical current conservation or numerical convergence promotion without evidence.
